description: The Fichiers fonciers are France's most detailed national description of land parcels, premises and ownership rights, derived from the DGFiP property tax files known as MAJIC. Since 2009 Cerema has reprocessed, geolocated and enriched them for the ministry in charge of housing, so public actors can run fine and comparable analyses. The data come as yearly vintages in two products: 16 main tables and aggregated tables such as commune tables and grids. Enrichments include owner classification, building typology, vacancy of a dwelling over a rolling five years and geolocation to the parcel; uses cited are land take, planning, housing, risk and energy. Coverage: all of France; latest vintage 2025. Access: public bodies request access on the Datafoncier portal, with a getting-started guide, a dictionary and training; Cerema publishes open derived tables such as vacant dwellings by commune and land take tables. Licence: restricted access, terms not read. Caveats: the data are built for taxation, so building characteristics follow tax rules, and personal data rules apply. Simulation uses are parcel-level building stock, age and vacancy for exposure, retrofit and land use models. Related records: the DVF transactions, Cartofriches and the BDNB national building database.
